evidence.claim: For a first comparison, the read sections give a Gaussian range-finder baseline, stabilized randomized subspace iteration, and a common compressed-matrix SVD postprocessing step.
The read §4.5 warns that unorthogonalized power iteration can lose small singular modes in floating point; compare the QR-stabilized scheme, not just the idealized matrix-power formula.

Algorithm 2 and §5.2 support block Krylov as a distinct iterative comparator. §8 reports a commodity-laptop experiment with 16 GB memory; this is the paper’s setting, not a result measured on the user’s laptop.
The read implementation section uses a larger Krylov subspace and extra QR/postprocessing work, so fewer iterations alone do not establish less runtime or memory on the user’s machine.

The 2023 preprint abstract and §2.1 identify non-Gaussian random-matrix families, including Rademacher and sparse Rademacher, making distribution choice a supported later comparison axis. No distribution-specific performance ranking is established by the material read.

The abstract says bounds have unspecified absolute constants, and §2.2 calls Procedure 1 idealized and vulnerable to roundoff. These sections do not give a ready numerical sample-count prescription or a stable implementation by themselves.

The read abstract describes RQRCP using a smaller random sample for pivot decisions, with truncated RQRCP feeding TUXV. It supports an optional rank-revealing-QR comparison lead; implementation details and speed claims have not been checked in the body.
